extracted.intended_audience: business and aviation industry readers, investors, and analysts
extracted.subtask_description: Analysis of Boeing's handling of technical failures, reliability, production and PR around the 787 Dreamliner; useful for evaluating aerospace crisis response and corporate communications. Summarizes performance, safety, fixes, supplier coordination and lessons learned.

rubrics_metrics.name: In-service dispatch reliability
rubrics_metrics.description: Boeing is committed to improving the 787's in-service dispatch reliability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Boeing says it is 'applying the resources required to achieve the results that we and our customers expect.' The company frames improving dispatch reliability as a measurable operational goal tied to customer expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Customer engagement and partnership
rubrics_metrics.description: Constant engagement with customers — partnering with them to prevent issues and helping them resolve them in the event they do occur.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Boeing emphasizes ongoing collaboration with airline customers as part of its response strategy, implying effective customer communication/support is a criterion for success.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify root cause and implement a permanent fix
rubrics_metrics.description: The cause of the battery failures were not precisely identified; however a permanent fix with multiple layers of protection was developed to ensure a maximum level of security.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The company and analysts stress the need for definitive root-cause analysis and engineering solutions that provide multiple levels of protection; lack of precise causation extends the time to full resolution ('it might take longer to solve').

rubrics_metrics.name: Absolute safety assurance
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain and emphasize the aircraft's safety (the company emphasized the aircraft's '100 percent safety').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public statements stressing safety are used to reassure customers and the public; safety is presented as the foremost non-negotiable criterion despite other operational issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Operational reliability targets and improvement
rubrics_metrics.description: Monitor and improve operational reliability metrics (e.g., 'Today, worldwide we are at 97 percent reliability. We are not pleased with that, we will improve that').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reliability percentages are cited as performance indicators; meeting or exceeding internal/industry benchmarks is treated as necessary for customer confidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timely delivery and meeting production targets
rubrics_metrics.description: Deliver aircraft on time and meet production/delivery schedules ('It's very important to deliver aircraft on time').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analysts note delivery targets can be unrealistic; consistent production rates are difficult but critical. Failure to meet schedules creates commercial and reputational problems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparent communication and PR management
rubrics_metrics.description: Manage media narratives and public perception effectively amid incidents ('PR fail or tech mess?' — heavy media attention on Dreamliner problems).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article highlights intense media coverage ('annus horribilis') and suggests that handling headlines, transparency and messaging are important to prevent reputational damage even when technical issues are addressed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigate and remediate incidents thoroughly
rubrics_metrics.description: Incidents such as battery overheating, on-board fires, and falling body panels must be investigated and causes resolved ('causes behind this accident still under investigation').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prompt, thorough investigation and corrective action are required for each incident to restore operational safety and customer confidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integrate lessons learned into program improvements
rubrics_metrics.description: Integrate lessons learned from previous rate increases and issues into a calculated and well-managed effort.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Boeing states it 'integrate[s] lessons learned... and fold[s] those into a calculated and well-managed effort' when adjusting production rates — institutional learning and process improvement are key criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplier coordination and supply-chain readiness
rubrics_metrics.description: Work closely with supplier partners to ensure parts, systems and people are in place for orderly change.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensuring suppliers can support production and fixes is highlighted as necessary to implement rate increases or corrective actions without creating further disruption.

rubrics_metrics.name: Set realistic expectations for new technology (anticipate teething problems)
rubrics_metrics.description: Expect revolutionary aircraft to have teething problems ('expecting an aircraft that is revolutionary in its scope to not have teething problems is madness').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analysts argue stakeholders should anticipate early problems with novel technology; managing expectations is a component of program evaluation and PR strategy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use existing programs as testbeds for future developments
rubrics_metrics.description: Treat the 787 as a laboratory for new technology that can be improved over its long lifetime and inform future models.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article notes the 787 provided lessons and technology applicable to future projects (e.g., 777X); ongoing updates and iterative improvements are part of program value.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain a broader product roadmap to mitigate competitive pressure
rubrics_metrics.description: Advance other models (e.g., announcement of the 777X variant) to ease focus away from single-model issues and pressure competitors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analysts suggest expanding or emphasizing other product lines can help offset reputational harm and competitive threats arising from problems with one model.
